structure:
Part 6 of 6, "Address Block and Change Log": the two closing sections of Confluence page "Live Animals & Germinals Data Fields - V4" version 210, read in full from the h1 'Address Block' (local-id cd92538a1b16, anchor macro address_block, byte 144,805 of .result.body) to the end of the body (the trailing empty paragraph local-id 674ac76e26b8). Nothing in the slice was sampled: it is 530 lines of pretty-printed storage HTML and every line was read. Layout of the slice, in page order: 1. h1 'Address Block' (the heading text sits in a highlight span, background rgb(198,237,251)), preceded only by two empty paragraphs that close part 5's germinal note. 2. One intro paragraph (local-id e5d45d2078d1) stating three rules: use the block where a field is described as Standard Address Block; the parent field determines whether an address record is required; the validation below applies once the address record is provided. It ends without a full stop. 3. The 'Address Block' table (ac:local-id 994fc687-87c3-43bc-9d4e-094b52a8af91, data-table-width 1502, 5 columns). Header row: Field Name | Attributes | Validation (header text carries a trailing space) | Example | Impacts. Note that this table does NOT carry the 8-column shape the page's other six tables use: it has no 'Type', 'Conditions / Values', 'Applies at:', 'Source' or separate 'Mandatory' column. The Mandatory/Optional marking lives in the Validation column, coloured red rgb(191,38,0) for Mandatory and green rgb(54,179,126) for Optional. 10 data rows, in order: Name or Organisation name, Transporter authorisation number (its cell is prefixed by a bare '**' and a line break), Address Line 1, Address Line 2, Town or city, County, Postal or Zip code, Country, Telephone number, Email address. Every field name is wrapped in . All 10 rows carry both an ANIMALS (Blue) and a GERMINALS (Green) status macro in Impacts — 20 status macros, no row marked for one journey only. No expand macro, no banner row, no anchor macro and no footnote anywhere in this table or after it. 4. h2 'Change Log' (local-id 6ff07a4de65b, bold, followed by two
). 5. The 'Change Log' table (ac:local-id cda48f2d-7067-49ea-8682-0ada02e75c96, data-table-width 1860, 3 columns). Header row: Field Name | Notes | Date. 8 data rows: Arrival time at port (anchor arrival_time_at_port), Journey Log (anchor journey_log), Transport after BCP (anchor transport_after_bcp), Animal Identifier - Wing Ring (anchor animal_identifier_wing_ring), 'Approved Establishment - germinals' (two spaces before the dash, no anchor), 'Package type - germinals' (wrapped in an inline-comment-marker, no anchor), 'Document Type list ', and 'Country of origin' (an external link back to this page's own #country_of_origin anchor). Six rows say 'de-scoped by' + a Confluence user mention; one says 'Updated List provided by' + a mention; one says 'updated to ‘mandatory to proceed’ as requested by' + a mention. Dates are elements: 2026-05-14 (x3), 2026-05-29, 2026-09-07 (x2), 2026-10-29, 2026-11-02. Every one of the eight mentions is the same account id. What this part covered: the Address Block intro's three rules, the table's 5 column names and field order, all 10 field rows claimed fact by fact (attributes with their length/format limit, Mandatory or Optional, the Example verbatim, the Impacts markers), the '**' marker on Transporter authorisation number, the Change Log's 3 columns and all 8 rows (six de-scopings and two changes), the judgement that at version 210 the page has no 'Out of Scope Data Elements' section so the Change Log's 'de-scoped by' rows are its out-of-scope record, and eight gap claims for what these two sections leave unsaid. Two slice-wide checks run with grep over the whole body: 'Out of Scope' appears 0 times on the page, and '**' appears exactly once on the page — the marker in this table — so no legend anywhere explains it. The page carries no page-level status macro, so no claim here rests on an unapproved decision.

claims.statement: At version 210 the page has no section titled "Out of Scope Data Elements"; the Change Log's six "de-scoped by" rows are the page's only record of what has been taken out of scope.
claims.ref: §Change Log (h2, local-id 6ff07a4de65b) and its table cda48f2d-7067-49ea-8682-0ada02e75c96; and the absence of any 'Out of Scope' heading in .result.body
claims.note: Follows from two checks over the whole page body: 'Out of Scope' appears 0 times, and the only de-scoping statements on the page are the six 'de-scoped by' rows of this table. So the de-scoped fields claimed in confluence-6497338582-p6-055 to -060 are the page's out-of-scope set: Arrival time at port, Journey Log, Transport after BCP, Animal Identifier - Wing Ring, Approved Establishment (germinals) and Package type (germinals).

claims.statement: The Change Log does not say who made any of its eight decisions in readable form: each Notes cell names the person only as a Confluence user mention, which the stored page records as an account id and not a name.
claims.ref: §Change Log, table cda48f2d-7067-49ea-8682-0ada02e75c96, Notes column of all 8 data rows
claims.note: All eight mentions carry the same ri:account-id, so one person is recorded as the author of every entry; the page as fetched does not resolve that id to a name.

claims.statement: The Change Log records no reason for any of the six de-scopings: each Notes cell says only "de-scoped by" and names a person, with no rationale, no replacement field and no ticket reference.
claims.ref: §Change Log, table cda48f2d-7067-49ea-8682-0ada02e75c96, Notes column of the six 'de-scoped by' rows

claims.statement: The Change Log records no entry for the Address Block itself — neither its addition nor any change to its ten fields — so the page gives no date for when the Standard Address Block's field list, limits or mandatory markings were last agreed.
